Revised by Henry Stuart Jones with Roderick McKenzie. 9th ed. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1940. Selected LSJ entry transcriptions were read at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy’s CLD and Scaife ATLAS on 8 September 2026. Other dictionaries displayed on the same page retain separate authorship. Cite headword, sense and the actual transcription. Primary passages cited inside a lexicon are leads until independently collated. The source **sources** lexical distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Those fields’ generated operations remain authorial register 3. ## Selected lexical witnesses ### q001 — Topos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes physical place, situated position, a passage in an author and a rhetorical topic. Aeschines 3.78 and Aristotle, Rhetoric 1358a14, are dictionary witnesses for distinct uses. These senses do not establish the authorial Arche-Topos compound or a mathematical theorem. **Locator:** s.v. τόπος, place/position, textual passage and rhetorical topic. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/τόπος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q002 — Logos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes reckoning, monetary accounts, account-giving, esteem, relation and mathematical ratio. Euclid V, definition 3, is cited for ratio. Their shared headword does not collapse their objects; the selected semantic range does not establish a complete philosophy of Logos. **Locator:** s.v. λόγος, LSJ I.1–4 and II.1–2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/λόγος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q003 — Nomos **Paraphrase:** The entry associates νόμος with νέμω and distinguishes customary usage from law or ordinance. The differently accented νομός has its own entry. This is lexical evidence, not proof of a compulsory pasture-to-state history or of the essay’s sixfold. **Locator:** s.v. νόμος, introduction and habitual practice/custom/law senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n71005/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q004 — Krisis **Paraphrase:** The entry derives the noun from κρίνω and distinguishes separating, judging, choosing and judicial proceedings. Its Aristotle Politics 1275a23 citation connects judgment and office within the cited civic context. The dictionary is the verified witness here; that Aristotelian passage has not been independently collated for this card. **Locator:** s.v. κρίσις, LSJ introductory and decision/judgment senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/κρίσις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q005 — Hybris **Paraphrase:** The initial sense concerns overbearing violence and insolence; the Odyssey suitors supply several cited examples. The semantic witness is narrower than Taylor’s exact theorem of a local determination occupying its determining condition. That theorem retains authorial standing; the lexicon does not independently derive it. **Locator:** s.v. ὕβρις, LSJ initial violence/insolence sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/ὕβρις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q006 — Anamnesis **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes calling to mind or recollection, reminders, a memorial sacrifice, and a separate lunar-return use. Its recollection citations include Plato, Phaedo 72e and 92d, Philebus 34c, and Aristotle, De memoria 451a21. These are dictionary witnesses; no complete Platonic argument is established by this card. **Locator:** s.v. ἀνάμνησις, introductory recollection sense and senses 2–3. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n7019/). **Verification:** entry read 2026-09-08; selected senses paraphrase-ready, ancient citation contexts and print edition not independently collated. **Consumer:** E2 recollection branch; the authorial return remains register 3. ### q007 — Homologia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes agreement and verbal consistency; assent, admission and concession; and compacts, including terms of peace or surrender. Plato, Symposium 187b and Theaetetus 164c, Aristotle, Topics 110a33, and the historical treaty citations are lexical witnesses here, not independently collated primary passages. The semantic range does not establish that every agreement is true, freely made or an instance of QL homology. **Locator:** s.v. ὁμολογία, agreement, admission and compact senses, including the peace/truce/surrender sub-sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n73748/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 historical Greek branch and homological-agreement office; evidence register 2, with the authorial comparison at register 3. ### q008 — Analogia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes mathematical and general proportion, analogy including grammatical analogy, relation, and correspondence or resemblance. Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics 1131a31, is a dictionary locator for the equality-of-ratios sense; Plato, Timaeus 31c–32c, is another cited witness. These primary passages were not independently collated. The range does not identify proportional analogy, focal predication and qualified predication as one historical doctrine. **Locator:** s.v. ἀναλογία, LSJ I–IV, including I.2 and II.2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n6926/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08 from the Scaife entry, retrieved via HTTP after the browsing tool's open error; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 analogy/Greek branches and C63's differentiated comparison grammars; evidence register 2, with the authorial coordination at register 3. The agreement and proportion entries **source** [E5’s Greek historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#e5-greek). The corresponding [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md) retains the project’s operational comparison at register 3. ### q009 — Νέμω — distribution and holding a portion **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes distributing portions, assigning honour or privilege, and middle-voice holding as one’s portion. Examples concern meat, property and land. These are attested semantic offices; the dictionary citations are not independently collated primary passages and do not establish a single chronology from pasture to state. **Locator and verification:** s.v. νέμω, distributive active and possessive middle senses; https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0057%3Aentry%3Dne%2Fmw ; read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry; print not collated. E6 branch E6-names consumes register-2 distribution/possession distinctions; its institutional return is register 3. The entry **sources** [E6’s historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md), with the institutional relation at register 3.

Translated by W. D. Ross. [Internet Classics Archive witness](https://classics.mit.edu/Aristotle/metaphysics.4.iv.html). Selected sections read on 8 September 2026: IV.2, opening health/medical/substance argument. The host identifies the translator; this receipt does not identify or collate a specific printed edition, Greek text or full work. The selected account **sources** [the historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). The historical proposition and Taylor’s relational operation retain distinct authority. ## Selected passages ### q001 — Multiple senses ordered to a primary reference **Paraphrase:** Healthy uses refer differently to health through preservation, production, indication or receptivity; medical uses likewise relate to an art. Aristotle coordinates different senses of being through a primary reference and identifies substance as the primary object of the inquiry. The differentiated relations belong to one investigation without having an identical definition or function. **Locator:** IV.2, opening argument; project locator 1003a33–1003b19. **Verification:** selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.

--- title: Owen — Lectures on Comparative Anatomy (1843) source_id: owen-1843-comparative-anatomy primary_domain: history-philosophy-science node_type: source-house record_type: scholarly-book ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: - Richard Owen title_full: Lectures on Comparative Anatomy, delivered at the Royal College of Surgeons in 1843 metadata_status: selected-witness-identified edition_status: local-scan-selected-text-checked citation_status: citation-ready-for-selected-witness-and-locator quote_status: paraphrase-ready; image-transcription-not-collated source_relation: Paraphrased local_copy: working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/owen/owen-1843-comparative-anatomy/owen.pdf passage_surface: '#passages' year: 1843 notes_taken_by: William White Cooper revised_by: Richard Owen --- # Lectures on Comparative Anatomy, delivered at the Royal College of Surgeons in 1843 The scan’s opening title names lectures delivered by Richard Owen, notes taken by William White Cooper and revision by Owen; Longman, Brown, Green, and Longmans, London, 1843. The E5 programme names the invertebrate-animal lectures. The selected witness is this 394-page scan, whose glossary supplies the consumed definitions. The opening title and embedded text at printed pp.374 and 379 were checked; no full-volume reading or image-level quotation transcription is claimed. [Acquired witness](https://darwin-online.org.uk/converted/pdf/1843_Owen_Lectures_A5436.pdf). Retrieved and selected text checked on 8 September 2026. Local SHA-256: `335ae0d425f2ba241794052b7f66228ceb77fe59dee07ccf35d8ea1c2aa5025b`. The witness **sources** [the historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** the historical comparison in its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Taylor’s generated operation remains distinct from the historical proposition. ## Selected passages ### q001 — Analogue **Paraphrase:** The definition identifies an analogue by an organ or part serving the same function in a different animal. **Locator:** Glossary, printed p.374; PDF page376. **Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim. ### q002 — Homologue **Paraphrase:** The definition identifies a homologue as the corresponding organ across animals despite variation in form and function. Read with the analogue entry, its anatomical criterion is distinct from shared function; neither definition itself establishes a modern common-descent criterion. **Locator:** Glossary, printed p.379; PDF page381. **Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim.

This is the stable source record for the project's Eckhart material: it carries the historical-philosophical account formerly split across a retired intake placeholder and the deprecated composite note. ## Chicago 18 forms **Full note:** Kurt Flasch, *Meister Eckhart: Philosopher of Christianity*, trans. Anne Schindel and Aaron Vanides (Yale University Press, 2015), {page}, https://yalebooks.yale.edu/9780300204865/meister-eckhart/. **Shortened note:** Flasch, *Meister Eckhart*, {page}. **Bibliography:** Flasch, Kurt. *Meister Eckhart: Philosopher of Christianity*. Translated by Anne Schindel and Aaron Vanides. Yale University Press, 2015. https://yalebooks.yale.edu/9780300204865/meister-eckhart/. ## Essay use ### Source's relevant contribution - A sustained philosophical reading of Eckhart's Latin and German works, including the argument of the *Opus tripartitum*, the Parisian questions, the Johannine commentary, the German sermons, and the *Book of Divine Consolation*. - A treatment of Eckhart's primary determinations, analogy and qualified predication, apophatic movement, the birth/ground material, and the metaphysics of the *verbum*. - A historically specific account of why Eckhart's theological language functions as philosophical argument rather than as a portable, decontextualised spirituality. ### Working content map - Chapters 6–11 follow the Latin project: its prologues, Parisian debates, programmatic speeches, Genesis, *In Sapientiam*, and *In Exodum*. - Chapter 13 (pp. 166–76) treats the Johannine commentary's method and its metaphysics of the *verbum*; chapter 14 continues the commentary's account of unity and likeness. - Chapters 15–17 return to the German sermons and the *Book of Divine Consolation*, including primary determinations, incarnation, and positive/negative theology. - The prior Eckhart note's leads—predicate and reversal, *in quantum* / “insofar as,” Word, image, ground, desert, and silence—belong in this book's content map. They await page-level extraction here; their previous omission from the record described a gap in the bank, not an absence from Flasch. ### Licensed essay use - Cite Flasch for his account of Eckhart's apophatic, predicative, analogical, and *verbum* problems; use the chapter and page locator appropriate to the assertion. - Carry Eckhart's predicate/reversal, ratio, Word, image, and apophatic-release movement into the formal-limit, zero, and Logos passages as a historically situated philosophical witness. ### Claim boundary - Flasch warrants a citation to Flasch's own historical-philosophical reading. A direct quotation from Eckhart, a claim about the wording of a particular sermon, or a contested philological decision needs the exact textual carrier and locator for that primary text. Those attribution requirements do not restrict the book's substantive coverage or displace Flasch from the current source chain. ## Consumption - **Stations:** §0/1/#3–4; §1; §4/#3; §5→0. - **Arguments:** [[Immutable Gap and Meta-Sign]]; [[Paradox as Cross-Register Hinge]]; [[Vāk]]. - **Source relation:** supplies the current historical-philosophical witness; page-level extracts will distinguish Flasch's analysis from direct Eckhart quotation. ## Quote and excerpt ledger | quote_id | exact text / excerpt file | locator | transcription | verification | consuming claim | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | — | No passage transcribed yet. | chapter/page locator needed | — | `locator-needed` | Use the working content map to extract the relevant Flasch passage before quoting; cite a primary carrier only for a direct Eckhart quotation or textual-critical claim. | ## Provenance and acquisition - **Metadata sources:** Yale University Press product page and Yale Scholarship Online / Oxford Academic chapter records, checked 2026-07-14. - **Text consulted:** official contents and chapter abstracts.
